inclusion_rule: Students who are not U.S. citizens or nationals and are in the United States on a visa or temporary basis without the right to remain indefinitely
explicit_exclusions: DACA recipients, undocumented students, and other eligible noncitizens are not reported in this category
comparison_warning: Do not treat this as a count of all international, immigrant-origin, undocumented, refugee, or foreign-born students

primary_source: Presidents' Alliance / Migration Policy Institute using U.S. Census Bureau CPS October Supplement
unit_of_analysis: Enrolled adults age 18-54 with at least a high school diploma or equivalent
inclusion_rule: First-generation immigrants plus second-generation immigrants; first generation includes naturalized citizens, permanent residents, refugees, asylees/asylum seekers, TPS recipients, undocumented people, and other domestic immigrant residents
explicit_exclusions: International students in the U.S. on nonimmigrant student visas for temporary study are excluded from the first-generation immigrant estimate
geography: National and state residence where supported
best_use: Measure domestic immigrant-origin participation in higher education
comparison_warning: This is a household-survey population estimate with a broader concept than IPEDS U.S. nonresident; the two series should not be added or substituted

primary_source: U.S. Department of Homeland Security SEVIS Data Mapping Tool via Higher Ed Immigration Portal
unit_of_analysis: SEVIS records at certified postsecondary institutions
inclusion_rule: Associates, bachelors, masters, and doctorate level international-student records at SEVIS-certified institutions
explicit_exclusions: Portal totals exclude vocational programs, primary/secondary school, flight school, and language training
geography: Institution/state/national views where SEVIS supports them
comparison_warning: SEVIS, Open Doors, and IPEDS use different timing, coverage, and reporting concepts; counts are not directly interchangeable

primary_source: Presidents' Alliance / American Immigration Council using ACS microdata
current_vintage: 2026 fact sheet; report-specific methodology controls exact vintage
inclusion_rule: ACS microdata are modeled to identify people likely to be undocumented and enrolled in postsecondary education; DACA-eligible students are estimated as a subset
explicit_exclusions: Potential international students are excluded using demographic, school-attendance, duration-of-stay, and work criteria
geography: National and state estimates where published
best_use: Estimate the scale and composition of undocumented college enrollment
comparison_warning: This is an estimated legal-status population, not an observed administrative category; do not compare one-for-one with IPEDS U.S. nonresident counts

primary_source: Presidents' Alliance / Migration Policy Institute using ACS plus NCES graduation rates
unit_of_analysis: Estimated undocumented youth reaching and completing high school
inclusion_rule: Undocumented high-school students under age 22 are estimated from ACS; differential graduation rates are then applied to estimate annual graduates
explicit_exclusions: This is not a cohort linkage to students later observed in higher education
geography: National estimate with supporting state/race/ethnicity inputs
best_use: Assess the potential higher-education access pipeline
comparison_warning: Do not interpret the annual graduate estimate as a transition rate into college or as the same population observed in higher-education enrollment data

measure_type: Population embedded within broader immigrant-origin measures
primary_source: Presidents' Alliance / Migration Policy Institute immigrant-origin framework
inclusion_rule: The first-generation immigrant category explicitly includes resettled refugees, asylees, and asylum seekers among other domestic immigrant groups
explicit_exclusions: The current project does not separately identify refugee/asylee students, and IPEDS U.S. nonresident is not a refugee-status measure
geography: National/state only when a population-specific source permits
best_use: Identify a documented measurement gap before making refugee-specific claims
comparison_warning: A refugee/asylee estimate requires a source designed to identify that status; neither the current IPEDS series nor the aggregate immigrant-origin total isolates it
